classes.pricedAsReason: A shares are not listed and, under the Novo Nordisk Foundation's articles, cannot be divested; the filings state no conversion right into B shares. They are priced at the B share price because both classes have the same DKK 0.10 nominal value and, per the Annual Report 2025, 'in practice, A and B shares receive the same amount of dividend per share'. This is a valuation convention, not a conversion.

notes: B shares are priced from the primary listing on Nasdaq Copenhagen (NOVO-B.CO, DKK) rather than the NYSE ADR (NVO, 1 ADR = 1 B share). B shares = 4,465,000,000 total A and B shares − 1,074,872,000 A shares − 58,755,131 treasury B shares = 3,331,372,869 at November 20, 2026, from Novo Nordisk's weekly buyback announcement filed on Form 6-K on November 23, 2026 (which states the total and the treasury holding but not the B count) and the 20-F cover's A-share count. Novo has been buying back B shares under a programme of up to DKK 15 billion running from February 4, 2026, so the 20-F count (3,390,128,000 B shares including treasury) is stale. Judgment call for review: the unlisted A shares are included at the B price; leaving them out would cut the value by about a quarter.
